notes.title: Exographer v57: Patch notes
notes.content:
Hi explorers. ScifunGames and Abylight Studios want to thank you for playing Exographer and your positive reviews. We are overwhelmed by the great reception of the game, and these help us to reach new players. Have you discovered the Natitan legacy yet? An exciting journey awaits. 

We are back to announce our second Exographer patch, with general improvements and bug fixes. Thanks for your feedback, it helps a lot with polishing, and making Exographer an even better game. We also updated our main art, to better communicate the style of gameplay: an exploration puzzle adventure, where players will be able to discover an exciting story, with characters, locations and powers based on particle physics. 

Please find down here every element we introduced with the latest patch:
Character 

Fixed a bug where the character animation freezes upon falling death.

World 

Initialization: Fixed a bug where the absurd matters were not the right ones, after finishing and restarting the game with the absurd matters inverted. 
General: Adjust the tablet opening based on where the character really is (temple, mirror, microscope, control room…) 
Mirror Room (level): The zinc rock clue can now be taken anytime in its three positions. 
Microscope (level): Raise some blue light intensity to be more visible.
Antichamber (level): Fixed a bug where the library button could be blocked by teleporting during animation. 
Academy (level): Ladder to microscope now stays deployed if powered.
Academy (level): Large zoom out now only triggers when interacting with the bench.
Cosmic (level): Fix the absurd matter exchange in the hidden zone.
Cosmic (level): Fixed a bug where the door leading to the charm cave was not activated anymore if the player teleported during animation. 
Yurt (level): Fixed a bug where opening the tablet while jumping in a particular place was leading to a black screen. 
Charm cave (level): Fixed a bug where opening the tablet in the secret area led to a black screen.
Charm cave (level): Fix a sprite of a broken magnet.
Strange yurt (level): Align the inside door position with the outside. 
Scintillating (level): Replace a visual water effect.
Muonic Sanctuary (level): The door to the secret level can now be triggered freely and the ladder is always deployed.
Muonic Sanctuary (level): The rosette lock can be reused after its first use to open and close the door. 
Control room (level): Fixed a bug where the automatic doors were not reacting well while taking pictures.
Control room (level): Added a Wedic dispenser for better quality of life.
Emulsive (level): Remove a random smoke.
Wedic station (level): Fixed a bug where the wheel could not be turned if player teleported during animation.
Lonely (level): Fixed a bug where you could send multiple Tungsten bars at the same time.
Lonely (level): Fixed a bug where the tracks were not displayed anymore after replacing the good tungsten bar.

Analyses

Unlocking the antipixule in the rosette can now trigger the ending scene.
Fixed a bug where the arrows are moving while using the chronogram and the antigram
Media and chronograms: Remove two rays to make the tutorials clearer.
Tutorial analysis - Fix a bug where the card is already selected
Cards and points of interest can be associated based on a larger overlap zone
Locked cards in the easy analysis mode are now trackable.  Route - Now displayed on already correct cards in easy mode
W Station: fixed the track sizes at the entry zoom level. 

User interface improvements

Large clue display: Hide arrows if it’s impossible to go next or previous.
Large clue display: Justify text to the left.
Rosette display: Handling the Shgig boson encrypted texts.
Page display: Allowing to go to the next or previous pages when the current page is not yet found. 
Navigation: Fixing the pre-selection on Dpad.
Larger button outlines on popup, main menu and pause menu.
Tablet: Change the close icon, not to mistake it with X.
Banner: Fixed a bug where the level banner displayed an encrypted version of the already discovered level.

Follow Abylight Studios on Steam (https://store.steampowered.com/publisher/Abylight) to get the latest news on our games, sales, bundles discounts and new releases.

notes.title: Devlog #10: Telling two stories
notes.content:
Exographer is primarily focused on its gameplay mechanics (see devlog #6), and its storyline emerged after all the design was essentially complete. Most of the text is used to solve puzzles, and it is revealed through the pages of a notebook to be decoded. To contextualize the information, each notebook entry is signed and dated by initially-mysterious characters... 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899177/1dc4f36e24e4642721504e86cf2f880509514c6c.png

In Exographer, the main character walks in the footsteps of nine academicians, rediscovering their discoveries and understanding why they disappeared. There are thus two stories: the one the character is living, and the one the academicians lived in the past. We've already covered this second storyline, based on the real history of science, in our devlog #4.

To visualize our character's typical journey through the academician world, as well as the flow of information the player receives, we used two interactive, non-linear storytelling tools. The first, Twine, is an open-source tool that lets you create such stories, like books in which you are the hero. A first version of our Exographer's story was conceived and proposed to the team by our narrative designer, Raphaël Granier de Cassagnac. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899177/5e94456e4d4aea1f59605e2a0299c1663253f5ab.png
We soon realized that this wouldn't be enough. While most of the notebook's pages focus on puzzles and include local clues, nine special pages require you to search for clues all over the world. Both for the players and the team could be confused by this apparent complexity! To visualize this scattered information, we used a second piece of software, ArcWeave, which, in addition to preserving the possible routes for the player, enabled us to add illustrations, lists of objects (pages, clues, academics...) and link them together. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899177/4db33d8848cfe1400775861c76307f6861b94379.png
If our players had access to our ArcWeave, they could easily answer the questions some of them have when platinizing the game, for example on Steam: 

Where to find Rofur and Tosom's codes for the emulsive zone? 
Where are Rucie’s, Shgig’s and Dirca's final clues hidden? 

But you better try to find them by yourself, it’s not that difficult.

notes.title: Exographer v56: Patch notes
notes.content:
Hi explorers. ScifunGames and Abylight Studios want to thank you for playing Exographer and your positive reviews. Have you discovered the Natitan legacy yet? An exciting journey awaits. 

We are back to announce our latest Exographer patch, version number 56, with general improvements and bug fixes. Thanks for your feedback, it helps a lot with polishing, and making Exographer an even better game. Please find down here every element we introduced with the latest patch:

Character

Fixed a bug where the player’s animation is frozen after loading a picture upon a death event.

World

Initialization: Fixed a bug where the absurd matters are not the right ones, after finishing the game with the absurd matters inverted, and then start a new game right away.
Source Antichamber (level): Added an absurd fog line to climb back if the player is aiming to complete its map.
Yurt (level): Fixed a bug where you cannot go up again if you reach the top and load the green fire picture.
Glowing Forge (zone): Enhance graphic visibility of platforms.
Greenhouse (level): Added a reset button for the whole line.
Zediacal Workshop (level): Fixed a bug where you leave the area with the glove unlocked, but not picked, resulting in being stuck in front of an absurd mud on your wayback.
Wedic Station (level): Fixed an arrow in the analysis so that the card matches the picture. 
Last Flooded Depth area: Added some insights and hints to help the player find the secret door entry.
Shattered Borders (zone): The thunder rhythm is now saved inside the last snap the player takes.
Waber’s Ascent (level): Fixed a bug where the automatic elevators are not reacting to the thunder anymore.
Lonely Experiment (level): Fixed a bug where the Tungsten bars line is locked when teleporting to a picture of this very level.

UI

Popup: Place the reticle on the first of the two buttons on a popup display.

Localization 

Chinese: Fixed two wrong Natitan names.

Achievements

Go high: include the falling part of the jump to be valid and unlock the achievement.

We are continuously working on enhancing the experience of playing Exographer. Remember to report anything you find through your gameplays, and we will fix it in upcoming patches. Thank you, again. 

This improvements and fixes are also available for Exographer on other platforms: Xbox, PS5, Epic Games and Nintendo Switch.

notes.title: DevLog #1: Graphic inspiration
notes.content:
In Exographer, the player's progress is punctuated by the discovery of elementary particles.
Most of Exographer's levels are graphically inspired by the actual scientific locations where these particles were discovered. We thought this was all the more appropriate given that these places are often gigantic, marvelous and photogenic.
These include, among others:

Particle colliders that are several kilometers long;
Cosmic ray observatories that lies in deserts;
Underground caverns that only neutrinos can reach...
In the very first level, the character even walks around in an old-fashioned television, because it was in this kind of cathode ray tube that the electron was discovered. The overall game's artistic direction was set on this first level. Several archaeo-scientific options were explored, and the most realistic was chosen (bottom right below).

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899177/35e75cb5fd62bb42958146e0c0d2fa9ea4f95026.png

Before tackling a new level, our graphic designer Thomas Vaulbert builds up a moodboard of past, present and future experiments that are related to the particle being discovered. He also talks to the physicists who work in these fascinating laboratories - it's even said that he visited CERN with the whole Exographer team at the start of the project…
Armed with all these images, he composes them into his own unique pixel art style. Some places really do resemble a specific location, like the neutrino pool at the Kamiokande mine in Japan (see below). Others are mixtures, extrapolations and interpretations.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899177/ecd5ca8673950bb455b9f3676f6b410ea7d97b43.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899177/794831da9d035975a5d8052f8adcb61d99b7084e.jpg
At the end, there will be more than 20 levels, all packed with references to real places.
